expectations.text: Rejects the 58-character trimming script

expectations.text: States that Google specifies no limit on the length of a title element
expectations.evidence: "Google states there's no length limit on <title>"

expectations.text: Explains that the title link is truncated in results to fit the device width, so a 50-60 character rule is lint rather than a pass/fail gate
expectations.evidence: "the truncation you see in results is a display constraint, not a ranking penalty for going over some cutoff"

expectations.text: Identifies the breadcrumb-shaped, brand-first title template as the reason Google is rewriting the title link
expectations.evidence: "Yours — Voltaic Docs - Guides - Webhooks - Sending a webhook — is the textbook case: four segments of navigation chrome before the one string a searcher actually typed. That shape, not the character count, is what's triggering the rewrite."

expectations.text: States that shortening the titles will not stop the rewriting
expectations.evidence: "Trimming to 58 characters keeps the same shape... You'd pay for 1,240 rewrites and see no change in the rewrite rate."

expectations.text: Prescribes a title template change in the Docusaurus config as one fix that reaches all 1,240 pages
expectations.evidence: "Rewrite the title template to {page} | Voltaic Docs | Docusaurus config / swizzled title component | ... | hours, one edit reaches all 1,240 pages"

expectations.text: Gives the target template shape with the specific page subject or searched term first and the product or brand last, for example {page} | {product} {section}
expectations.evidence: "Target | Send a webhook | Voltaic Docs"

expectations.text: Rejects adding the product name to the start of every h1, and explains that it stops the h1 describing the page and hands the rewriter another unhelpful source
expectations.evidence: "Prefixing \"Voltaic\" onto every h1 hands the rewriter more brand-first, boilerplate-shaped text to pull from... It also stops the h1 from doing its actual job: telling a reader (and Google) what the page is about."

expectations.text: Names at least two of the sources Google may build a replacement title link from: headings, og:title, prominent styled text, other page text, inbound anchor text, or WebSite structured data
expectations.evidence: "Google will keep building its own title from your h1, headings, and anchor text, exactly as it does now."
